plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do. This ensures you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (maximizing profit) and never overpay (never lose money) when you do win. Since payment equals the second-highest bid, not my own bid, there's no benefit to shading below value. I'll bid exactly my value of $31.

In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of opponents' strategies. This is because if I bid below my value, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won; if I bid above my value, I risk winning at a price higher than my value, causing a loss. Since payment depends only on the second-highest bid (not my own bid, given I win), bidding exactly my value maximizes expected profit. With value $31, I will bid $31.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their behavior. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so bidding your value maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying or losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $46, I will bid exactly $46 to ensure optimal outcomes.
